name: Time parked per residential/parcel customer (unload, walk, proof of delivery)
note: Mean 4.1, min 1.6, max 6.8 across 25 accompanied parcel rounds; 72 customers and 37 parking stops per round, so 8.1 min per parking stop. Central London, mixed residential/commercial; US suburban doorstep drops likely sit toward the low end.
source_name: Allen et al. (2018), Understanding the impact of e-commerce on last-mile light goods vehicle activity in urban areas: the case of London, Transportation Research Part D 61(B), Table 4

name: Time at stop for an oversized (furniture/large) drop, no install
note: Kim et al.: oversized supplies (furniture, construction materials) averaged 20 min vs 14-18 for other goods; two-or-more-worker deliveries also 20 min. Low = all-delivery median 12.3; high = 29 min mean for multi-destination deliveries. Downtown commercial buildings, used as proxy for residential bulky.
source_name: Kim, Goodchild & Boyle (2021), Empirical analysis of commercial vehicle dwell times around freight-attracting urban buildings in downtown Seattle, Transportation Research Part A 147 (UW Urban Freight Lab)

name: Dwell per commercial delivery (vehicle parked, out-of-vehicle time)
note: Median 12.3, mean 16.4, IQR 7.8-21.1 over 157 observed deliveries at five downtown Seattle buildings. Passenger-vehicle deliveries ~8 min; documents shorter. Use median as value (right-skewed).
source_name: Kim, Goodchild & Boyle (2021), Empirical analysis of commercial vehicle dwell times around freight-attracting urban buildings in downtown Seattle, Transportation Research Part A 147 (UW Urban Freight Lab)

name: Dwell per commercial delivery (restaurant/retail drop)
note: Mean 16.4 (truck/van with roll-up or swing doors ~17); IQR low 7.8; high = 29 min mean for multi-destination deliveries. Kim also cites UK guidance of 20 min per rigid HGV delivery and Morris (2004) NYC docks 31.5 min mean.
source_name: Kim, Goodchild & Boyle (2021), Empirical analysis of commercial vehicle dwell times around freight-attracting urban buildings in downtown Seattle, Transportation Research Part A 147 (UW Urban Freight Lab)

name: Free time per stop for an LTL delivery under 2,500 lb (proxy for liftgate pallet service)
note: Tariff free time = what carriers price as normal unload time. Central Transport: <2,500 lb 30 min, 2,500-4,999 lb 60 min. Low 15 = AAA Cooper <=2,500 lb (Magnum LTL <1,000 lb also 15). A contractual allowance, not a stopwatch measurement.
source_name: Central Transport Rules Tariff 100-CC, Item 500 detention free time

name: Unload time per stop, palletized building material (tariff proxy)
note: Derived proxy: same LTL tariff free-time schedule (Central Transport 30 min <2,500 lb, 60 min 2,500-4,999 lb; AAA Cooper 15 min <=2,500 lb). Jobsite boom/forklift drops have no published time study found.
source_name: Central Transport Rules Tariff 100-CC, Item 500 detention free time

name: Time at stop for two-person delivery with standard install
note: Vendor ranges: delivery-only 5-15 min; standard install (range, top-load washer, dryer) 30-60; complex (built-in fridge, dishwasher, front-load washer) 60-120; premium 120-180. Value = midpoint of standard install.
source_name: Upper Route Planner blog, Variable service times by appliance type (vendor, updated 2026-05-01)

name: Forklift time to load one pallet onto a truck
note: Single-pallet forklift cycle 90 s (26 pallets x 90 s = 39 min for a 53 ft trailer). Low/high are practitioner range around that cycle; pallet-jack loading of a box truck runs slower.
source_name: Racklify encyclopedia, Quad pallet handler: definition, uses and operational basics (vendor reference)

name: Forklift time to load one pallet onto a truck
note: Same 90 s single-pallet cycle; mixed lumber/bundles add strapping time.
source_name: Racklify encyclopedia, Quad pallet handler: definition, uses and operational basics (vendor reference)

name: Forklift time to load one pallet onto a P&D trailer
note: Same 90 s single-pallet cycle.
source_name: Racklify encyclopedia, Quad pallet handler: definition, uses and operational basics (vendor reference)

name: Dwell per pickup or delivery at shipper/receiver
note: ATRI uses 2 h of presumed active operations (67% of carriers start detention at 2 h). In 2023 drivers saw dwell beyond 2 h at 39.3% of stops and >2 h of detention at 9.9%. Low 1.0 = R+L tariff free time for a pallet-loaded 10,000-20,000 lb vehicle stop. High 3.4 = 2 h + VTTI/FMCSA 2014 mean detention of 1.4 h per detained stop (cited in the ATRI report).
source_name: ATRI, Costs and Consequences of Truck Driver Detention (Sept 2024), 2023 data

name: Marine terminal truck turn time (queue entry to exit gate)
note: 84 min combined LA/LB average, May 2017 (LA 82, LB 87). Low 33 min (Matson LB), high 139 min (TTI). Old data; HTA has published monthly since.
source_name: Transport Topics, Truck turn times lengthen in May at Ports of Los Angeles, Long Beach (Harbor Trucking Association GPS data)

name: Average downtown trip speed
note: Derived mean of the ten US downtown speeds INRIX lists (NYC 13, Chicago 14, LA 22, Boston 13, Philadelphia 14, Miami 20, Houston 17, Atlanta 18, DC 12, Seattle 18). Car speeds; a box truck will be slower.
source_name: INRIX 2024 Global Traffic Scorecard, US press release (downtown speeds)

name: Average metro-wide trip speed (all roads)
note: Derived from TomTom 2025 Minneapolis metro: 10 km in 12 min 46 s = 47.0 km/h = 29.2 mph. Low = rush-hour average 39 km/h (24.2 mph). High = midnight 10 km in 11 min 20 s (32.9 mph). One metro used as a stand-in for US suburban.
source_name: TomTom Traffic Index 2025, Minneapolis MN metro

name: Average truck speed on Interstates (peak period)
note: Derived mean of the 25 Interstates' peak-period speeds (2009). Low = I-5 peak 52.0; high = I-20/I-25 non-peak 59.3. Metro Interstates run slower: 2012 FF&F Table 3-17 averaged 51.6 mph across 14 metros (LA 43.0).
source_name: FHWA Freight Facts and Figures 2010, Table 3-8 Average truck speeds on selected Interstate highways: 2009

name: Average truck speed on Interstates (peak period)
note: Same 2009 table; low widened to 43.0 = LA metro Interstate truck average 2012 (FF&F 2013 Table 3-17), since port drays run metro freeways.
source_name: FHWA Freight Facts and Figures 2010, Table 3-8 Average truck speeds on selected Interstate highways: 2009

name: Pre-trip inspection logged as on-duty not driving
note: No federal time requirement; FMCSA requires only that it be logged as on-duty not driving. Source gives 10 and 12 min as worked examples; 15 min is the common driver-school allowance.
source_name: HeavyVehicleInspection.com, Hours of service: pre-trip inspection time (trade explainer)

name: Customer arrival window for scheduled home delivery
note: Vendor notes the generic 4-hour block and recommends 30-minute windows.
source_name: Upper Route Planner blog, Variable service times by appliance type (vendor, updated 2026-05-01)

name: Consignee receiving window (business hours)
note: Tariff business hours Monday-Friday 8:00 am-5:00 pm (9 h); deliveries outside them pay an after-hours charge (Item 754). Low 1 h = appointment delivery (Item 647, notification/appointment fee), estimate.
source_name: Central Transport Rules Tariff 100-CC, Item 500 detention free time

name: Jobsite/yard receiving window
note: Derived: B2B business-hours window per LTL tariff (8-5). Contractor 'first thing AM' asks narrow it; no published study found.
source_name: Central Transport Rules Tariff 100-CC, Item 500 detention free time

name: Restaurant/retail receiving window
note: Derived: B2B business-hours window per LTL tariff (8-5). Restaurant receiving before lunch service narrows it; no published study found.
source_name: Central Transport Rules Tariff 100-CC, Item 500 detention free time

name: Same-day courier delivery window
note: Derived: business-hours window per LTL tariff (8-5); rush/2-hour courier service tiers narrow it. No published US courier study found.
source_name: Central Transport Rules Tariff 100-CC, Item 500 detention free time

name: Lateness tolerated before a delivery counts late
note: LTL on-time is scored by service day: delivered on the scheduled day = on time (Old Dominion reports 99% on-time on that basis). Within-day lateness is not penalized; model as a day-level flag.
source_name: Old Dominion Freight Line Q4 2024 earnings release

name: Parcel first-attempt delivery failures
note: 100 - 99.22% US first-attempt success, Q2 2025 = 0.78%. High 2.8 = 100 - 97.2% US first-attempt success (Parcel Monitor via SmartRoutes).
source_name: Parcel Perform, United States delivery performance Q2 2025

name: First-attempt failures, attended home delivery
note: 'The failure rate for first attempted home deliveries is 7.6%, but this rate more than doubles for the second and third attempted deliveries.' Southeast Asian carrier data; attended (signature/presence) deliveries. Low 2.8 = US parcel figure; high 15.2 = 2 x 7.6, since the same source says the rate more than doubles on second and third attempts (use for redelivery stops).
source_name: Choo (2016), Impact of a Delivery Point Network (SUTD thesis; carrier data)

name: Empty miles as share of total
note: ATRI 2025 (2024 data): 'empty miles rose to an average of 16.7 percent.' Low 16.3 = 2024 report (2023 data), all non-tank operations. Regional/dedicated fleets vary well beyond this band; widen if a scenario needs it.
source_name: ATRI, New ATRI report shows trucking profitability severely squeezed (Operational Costs of Trucking 2025, 2024 data)

name: Bobtail/chassis miles as share of total
note: Derived: CARB O-D survey, 33.2 mi per loaded trip to transload/local DC, 20.6 mi per bobtail/chassis trip; 20.6/(20.6+33.2) = 38.3%. Low 8.9% = bobtail share of miles for a Chicago cross-town dray fleet before dispatch optimization (fell to 4.7% after), FHWA C-TIP.
source_name: California Air Resources Board, Drayage truck regulation Appendix B/F (2007), Table II-7 and cost analysis

name: Loaded miles per tractor per operating day
note: Derived: FHWA VM-1 2023 combination trucks average 58,890 mi/yr; / 250 operating days = 235.6 mi/day; x (1 - 0.167 ATRI 2025 deadhead) = 196 loaded. Low 185 = same over 265 days. High 236 = all 235.6 mi/day loaded (zero deadhead bound). The 250-day year is an assumption.
source_name: FHWA Highway Statistics 2023, Table VM-1 (updated March 2025)

name: Route miles per single-unit truck per operating day
note: Derived: FHWA VM-1 2023 single-unit trucks 11,593 mi/yr / 250 days = 46.4. Local routes run loaded out and empty back, so this is total route miles. Low/high = +/-25%, estimate.
source_name: FHWA Highway Statistics 2023, Table VM-1 (updated March 2025)

name: P&D miles per single-unit truck per operating day
note: Derived: FHWA VM-1 2023 single-unit 11,593 mi/yr / 250 days = 46.4 total. Low/high +/-25%, estimate.
source_name: FHWA Highway Statistics 2023, Table VM-1 (updated March 2025)

name: Route miles per single-unit truck per operating day
note: Derived: FHWA VM-1 2023 single-unit 11,593 mi/yr / 250 days = 46.4 total. Low/high +/-25%, estimate.
source_name: FHWA Highway Statistics 2023, Table VM-1 (updated March 2025)

name: Loaded miles per dray truck per day
note: Derived: CARB assumes 2.4 container moves/day x 33.2 loaded mi per transload/local trip = 79.7. Low = 2.4 x 20 mi (off-dock rail) = 48. Total incl. bobtail = 2.4 x 53.8 = 129 mi/day.
source_name: California Air Resources Board, Drayage truck regulation Appendix B/F (2007), Table II-7 and cost analysis

name: Road miles / straight-line miles
note: Ballou et al. 2002: United States 1.20 (s.d. 0.17); US East 1.20, US West 1.21. Low/high = +/-1 s.d. (derived).
source_name: MIT CTL.SC1x lecture, One-to-many distribution (reproducing Ballou, Rahardja & Sakai 2002, Transportation Research Part A 36(9):843-848)

name: Route miles per single-unit truck per operating day
note: Derived: FHWA VM-1 2023 single-unit trucks 11,593 mi/yr / 250 days = 46.4. Local routes run loaded out and empty back, so this is total route miles. Low/high = +/-25%, estimate.
source_name: FHWA Highway Statistics 2023, Table VM-1 (updated March 2025)

name: Route miles per single-unit truck per operating day
note: Borrowed from the single-unit-truck figure (FHWA VM-1 2023, 11,593 mi/yr / 250 days = 46.4); no van-specific courier daily-miles source found. Used only to size the practice map.
source_name: FHWA Highway Statistics 2023, Table VM-1 (updated March 2025)
